RISKS.t: Passenger personal data open to any caller
RISKS.d: /analytics/Passenger and /processor/Passenger return FirstName, LastName, Street, PhoneNumber, EMailAddress without a role check; with no service-level @requires this may include unauthenticated calls (verify behind the approuter).
RISKS.test: GET /analytics/Passenger, /processor/Passenger as anonymous and as a user without roles, expect 401/403.

RISKS.t: TravelAgency personal data open to any caller
RISKS.d: /analytics/TravelAgency and /processor/TravelAgency return Street, PhoneNumber, EMailAddress without a role check; with no service-level @requires this may include unauthenticated calls (verify behind the approuter).
RISKS.test: GET /analytics/TravelAgency, /processor/TravelAgency as anonymous and as a user without roles, expect 401/403.

RISKS.t: rejectTravel, acceptTravel callable in states the UI hides
RISKS.d: @Core.OperationAvailable hides rejectTravel when TravelStatus != X; acceptTravel when TravelStatus != A, but no handler checks the status, so a direct POST still changes it.
RISKS.test: POST each action on an instance in the hidden state, expect 4xx.

RISKS.d: Every entity under /analytics is readable by any caller (CAP default restrict_all_services: false).
RISKS.test: GET /analytics/$metadata and one entity set as anonymous.

RISKS.d: UI: TravelStatus = O. Server: allows TravelStatus in {X, O}; also X. The server lets X through.
RISKS.test: Call deductDiscount in the states the UI hides, expect 4xx.

RISKS.t: Tests run as one user only (alice)
RISKS.d: 4 grants exist, but no existing test runs as a user who should be denied, so a broken @restrict would pass.
RISKS.test: Role × operation tests from the authorization matrix (generated).

RISKS.t: Read-only and hidden-create rules exist only in the UI (5)
RISKS.d: Travel: 5 fields controlled by TravelStatus.fieldControl; Booking: 6 fields controlled by to_Travel.TravelStatus.fieldControl; Booking: hidden when [object Object]; Booking: hidden when [object Object]; BookingSupplement: 4 fields controlled by to_Travel.TravelStatus.fieldControl. OData clients can still PATCH, POST or DELETE.
RISKS.test: PATCH a locked field and POST/DELETE a child on a non-open instance, expect 4xx.

RISKS.d: app/common.cds annotates built-in cds.UUID for the whole model: every element of that type in every service changes, including ones the author never saw.
RISKS.test: Check $metadata of each service for the annotation on unrelated cds.UUID fields.

RISKS.t: createTravelByTemplate declared and granted, no handler
RISKS.d: The action is in the service and reachable through OData, but no Node handler implements it; CAP answers with an error at runtime.
RISKS.test: POST createTravelByTemplate as an authorised user, expect a defined error or remove the action.

RISKS.t: Booking / BookingSupplement: access inherited from the draft root
RISKS.d: Composition children carry no own @restrict. Access through the root is checked; direct requests to the child set need a test.
RISKS.test: PATCH a child as a user without write access on the root, expect 403.

RISKS.t: 3 CDS files change models of another layer
RISKS.d: app/travel_processor/field-control.cds: extends domain TravelStatus; srv/analytics-service.cds: annotates domain Airport; srv/analytics-service.cds: annotates domain FlightConnection.
RISKS.test: Architecture test on the CDS dependency graph (fails on new violations).

RISKS.d: no-outdated-manifest-version, no-deprecated-api. These break with the next UI5 major release.
RISKS.test: Run @ui5/linter in CI and fail on errors.

RISKS.d: When the travel is gone, the error message reads travel.ID from undefined: a TypeError and a 500 instead of a 404.
RISKS.test: deductDiscount on a deleted TravelUUID, expect 404 with message.

RISKS.d: max(TravelID) is read and incremented on CREATE. Two parallel activations can get the same ID.
RISKS.test: Activate two drafts in parallel, assert distinct TravelIDs.

RISKS.d: All FlightPrices are summed as USD regardless of their currency.
RISKS.test: Seed a EUR booking, assert aggregation either converts or groups by currency.

SECTIONS.name: Architecture
SECTIONS.take: 2 UI5 apps on 2 OData services, served by one CAP Node.js process with 13 handlers. 7 business rules are promised by UI annotations only, not enforced by the server.

SECTIONS.name: Data model
SECTIONS.take: 13 entities: 3 in draft documents, 7 master data, 3 code lists. Personal data in Passenger, TravelAgency.

SECTIONS.name: Dependencies
SECTIONS.take: 15 CDS files, 23 file-to-file dependencies. 3 reach past their layer, 4 put UI annotations straight on the domain.

SECTIONS.name: Data flow & events
SECTIONS.take: 3 entities get fields written by handlers; the busiest handler is on deductDiscount Travel (travel-service.ts:97). 6 lifecycle events carry server or UI hooks.

SECTIONS.name: TravelStatus lifecycle
SECTIONS.take: 3 states, 9 action × state pairs. The UI allows 5, the Node server 8; 3 disagree.

SECTIONS.name: Authorization
SECTIONS.take: 6 users (anonymous plus mock users) × 13 operations. 4 operations expose personal data without a role. 6 cells are exercised by existing tests.

SECTIONS.name: Coding patterns
SECTIONS.take: 32 patterns found by fixed detectors. 2 cause a defect or exposure, 6 work but sit in the wrong place.

SECTIONS.name: UI promises vs server
SECTIONS.take: 21 rules the UI promises, read from the annotations. 13 are enforced by the server or by CAP, 1 only partly; 7 exist only in the UI and can be bypassed with a plain OData call.

SECTIONS.name: UI tests
SECTIONS.take: 22 UI checks generated from 8 UI promises (9 app starts, OPA5 + sap.fe.test), not run yet. 9 states are guarded by the UI only; 8 promises are not testable in the UI (reasons listed).

SECTIONS.name: Risks
SECTIONS.take: 15 risks: 12 found by rules, 3 by agent review. Highest: Passenger personal data open to any caller (score 16).

SECTIONS.name: Rules from agent findings
SECTIONS.take: 13 rules drafted from agent findings: 0 accepted, 13 waiting for review. 4 drafts fire on this app, reproducing agent findings A12, A8, A7 without AI.

SECTIONS.name: Test design
SECTIONS.take: 122 equivalence classes in 7 categories; 12 covered by existing tests. deductDiscount: 19 all-pairs cases instead of 216.

SECTIONS.name: Coverage by class
SECTIONS.take: 16 of 122 classes tested (13%) by tests that ran in CI; 7 pin today's behaviour with the intended one waiting as a spec test, 0 generated but not run yet, 41 likely (approximate match), 58 untested.

SECTIONS.name: Interfaces
SECTIONS.take: 2 service roots, 23 entity sets, 4 actions. 20 sets need no role, including personal data.

SECTIONS.name: Runtime check
SECTIONS.take: The running app (cds 10.1.0) registered 13 handlers from its own code: 13 match what the static parser found. Service paths: 2 of 2 as predicted. Plugins registering handlers: @cap-js/db-service.

SECTIONS.name: Measured in CI
SECTIONS.take: Authorization: CAP answered 66 requests; 61 cells agree with the static matrix, 5 settle an unclear cell. Tests sent 110 requests from 4 test files as 6 users. Rules reached by any test: 9 of 11 (2 never run).

rules.from: stress corpus AI pass (2026-11-02): emit lost in a refactoring

rules.title: Currency hard-coded where amounts are aggregated or returned

hits.d: srv/analytics-service.cds:24: The literal 'USD' is used as the currency. Amounts in other currencies are then labelled (and summed) as USD.

rules.title: Sequential id from max() + 1 (race under parallel requests)

hits.d: srv/travel-service.ts:18: req.data.TravelID is set from a max() query + 1 in a shared code path. Two requests that read max() before either commits get the same value; without a unique constraint both rows are stored.

rules.title: Error path reads a property of the value it just found missing

hits.t: travel.$P read where travel is missing
hits.d: srv/travel-service.ts:105: `if (!travel)` then reads `travel.$P`. travel is null or undefined on that path, so the request fails with a TypeError (HTTP 500) instead of the intended error.
